About the role 

DekkoSecure is an international technology company with deep expertise in protecting highly sensitive and mission critical data. DekkoSecure's focus is building military-grade, end-to-end encrypted security workflow solutions for government, law enforcement agencies, defence primes, and the enterprise healthcare sector. Our product suite includes DekkoCORE, a highly secure platform for file sharing and collaboration, and DekkoDEMS, purpose-built for digital evidence management. As we scale, we are creating a dedicated Business Systems Analyst position to sit at the centre of our product, support, commercial and operations functions. 

The Business Systems Analyst is responsible for eliciting and documenting business and system requirements, analysing existing processes and data, and translating client and internal needs into clear functional specifications and improved system functionality. The role is the central reference point between platform users, the product and engineering teams, and the wider business, ensuring that changes to our systems and processes are well specified, tested and adopted. 

Key responsibilities 

We are seeking an engaging, organised and analytical individual with advanced written and verbal communication skills who can: 

 * Work with platform users, clients and internal teams to draw out what they need from DekkoSecure’s systems, pin those needs down precisely, and write them up as requirements that both the business and the engineering team can build against. 

* Engage with users and clients across the company’s Australian, Northern European and North American markets to elicit, formulate and document business and system requirements, and to analyse how the platform is used in each market. 

* Examine how work currently flows through the company’s support, onboarding and data-handling activities and build process and data maps that expose where the business loses time, drops information or breaks down. 

* Analyse client usage of the platform to identify adoption patterns, friction points and where users encounter difficulty or inefficiency, feeding these findings back to the product and engineering teams with recommendations for improvement. 

* Weigh the available options and put forward the process changes and system behaviour the business should adopt, ranking each recommendation by the value it returns and the number of users it affects. 

* Turn agreed requirements into functional specifications the product and engineering teams can build from, across both DekkoCORE and DekkoDEMS. 

* Apply data and process modelling techniques to design and document how information and processes flow across core business systems, establishing and maintaining a single source of truth. 

* Set the test plans and acceptance criteria each change has to pass and run that testing, so nothing reaches production or client use until it holds up against the agreed requirements. 

* Run analysis and implementation work as planned, costed and resourced initiatives using agile methods, including the programmes to consolidate the company’s systems and formalise its processes, and track them through to delivery. 

* Design and maintain reporting and forecasting dashboards that give leadership accurate, data-driven visibility of system and operational performance. 

* Create and maintain documentation, including internal standard operating procedures for staff and external user guides and Help Center content for clients. 

* Conduct training and structured walkthroughs of new and changed platform functionality for internal users and clients to support adoption and validate that delivered changes meet acceptance criteria. 

* Be the person the business turns to on how its systems and processes work, advising the product, support, commercial and operations teams when they need to make system or process decisions. 

Skills, qualifications, experience required 

* A relevant tertiary qualification in information technology, business informatics, or a related cross-functional business and information technology discipline. A postgraduate qualification combining information technology and business is highly regarded. 

* Experience working in a start-up or scale-up environment in a client-facing role. 

* Willingness to undertake occasional international travel to Europe and North America for requirements gathering. 

* Ability to understand user and client needs and translate them into documented system and process requirements. 

* Demonstrated ability to translate user and client needs into documented system and product improvements within a software or SaaS environment. 

* Experience with CRM systems, document and collaboration platforms. 

* Competence in data and process modelling, and in producing clear system specifications and process documentation. 

* Experience preparing and delivering user training. 

* Strong stakeholder management skills across technical and non-technical teams. 



Desirable 

* Exposure to secure collaboration, document management or cybersecurity software products. 

* Familiarity with project management methodologies (for example Agile) and supporting tools. 

* Experience supporting product roadmap decisions through structured feedback and analysis. 

How to apply 

Applications must be submitted through this advertisement. Please include a current resume and a short cover letter addressing the essential skills and experience above. Applications are open to Australian citizens and permanent residents and to other candidates with valid work rights in Australia.
result.title: Business Systems Analyst

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Nurse-Midwife Educator Emergency



 Apply now
 Job no: 940184

 Work type: Part time

 Location: Rural Support Service

 Categories: Nursing-Midwifery





 

Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network 

Regional Support Services - Adelaide Metro Area 

Salary: Salary: RN-M3C $130,190 p.a. to $136,010 per annum (adjusted to actual hours worked) 

Ongoing, Part Time (12 hours per week-0.32 FTE) 

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

The Nurse-Midwife Educator Emergency plays a key role in strengthening emergency nursing and midwifery capability across the health service by providing education, training, and professional support to clinicians. Drawing on at least three years of post-registration clinical experience, the role contributes to the development of learning experiences, educational resources, and local teaching initiatives that enhance clinical knowledge, confidence, and practice. The position manages the Regional Emergency Nursing and Midwifery Education (ENAME) program, supports regional emergency service programs and nurses and midwives working in regional emergency departments, helping to build a skilled and responsive workforce. 

In addition to education delivery, the role provides leadership in the coordination of projects, programs, and research aimed at improving educational outcomes and service delivery. The Nurse-Midwife Educator Emergency is accountable for promoting safe, evidence-based practice, addressing gaps between policy and practice, and fostering a positive workplace culture that supports high-quality patient and client outcomes. Through collaboration, mentorship, and project leadership, the role contributes to continuous improvement and the delivery of effective emergency care across the network.

WHO ARE WE? 

The RSS is a business unit in SA Health and provides services throughout regional South Australia to support the six regional local health networks (LHNs). It employs around 260 people who work in 37 regional, rural and remote SA locations, or in the RSS's three Adelaide offices. 

 WHERE AND HOW YOU WILL WORK 

Many RSS staff enjoy working from home or remotely and benefit from the work-life balance this provides. They enjoy the freedom to further their career while remaining part of their local community and contributing to health care right across regional South Australia. 

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

Are you passionate about developing the next generation of emergency nurses and midwives and supporting clinicians to deliver exceptional patient care? 

Do you thrive in a role where you can influence workforce capability, lead education initiatives, and drive positive change across diverse clinical settings? 

Can you inspire, coach, and mentor others while building strong relationships with clinicians, managers, students, and key stakeholders? 

Are you committed to evidence-based practice, innovation, and continuous improvement, using research and contemporary knowledge to enhance learning outcomes? 

Do you enjoy leading projects and collaborating across teams to improve education, workforce development, and emergency care services for regional communities? 

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will.... 

Lead and deliver high-quality emergency nursing and midwifery education programs, including teaching, assessment, clinical education support, and workforce capability development across regional and local services. 

Coordinate and support learning and professional development initiatives for clinicians, students, and multidisciplinary teams, ensuring contemporary, evidence-based practice is embedded into clinical care. 

Drive education projects, service improvement activities, and change management initiatives that enhance workforce capability, patient outcomes, and organisational performance. 

Provide expert clinical and professional leadership, acting as a mentor, consultant, and trusted advisor to managers, educators, and clinicians on professional practice, workforce development, and education strategies. 

Promote best practice through research, innovation, and continuous improvement, integrating current evidence into education programs and supporting the development of a positive, safe, and high-performing clinical culture. 

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways: 

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information 

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities. 

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program. 

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families. 

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS? 

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following: 

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy. Further information is in the application for to help guide you. 

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. We continually look for ways to support and promote diversity and flexible ways of working so please let us know what interests you. 

NEED TO RELOCATE? 

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. See what is available here: Relocation support | SA Health. Find out more about working in the Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network, and see what it looks like to work and live in regional Australia at: https:--movetomore.com.au-

NVD Fresh Produce Pty Ltd
Walkaway, Western Australia

Full Time Truck Driver 
(2 Positions Available)

Salary
AUD $100,000 – $110,000 per annum plus Superannuation, depending on skills and experience.

About us:
NVD Fresh Produce Pty Ltd is a family-owned agricultural enterprise based in Walkaway, Western Australia, approximately 30 minutes from Geraldton. We operate approximately 4.2 hectares of plastic greenhouses in Walkaway and an additional 2 hectares of plastic greenhouses at the family’s original farm.

We are currently expanding our operations, having purchased 60 acres of land near Walkaway to support future growth and long-term sustainability. NVD Fresh Produce specialises in intensive greenhouse cultivation and is progressively diversifying its crop range, recognising crop rotation as a key strategy to preserve soil health, improve productivity, and maintain consistent supply.

The business is focused on strengthening its production capacity, improving operational systems and water management practices, and establishing a scalable and sustainable structure to support ongoing expansion within Western Australia’s fresh produce market.

The successful applicant will play an important role in supporting the continued growth and success of NVD Fresh Produce's farming operations.

Position Summary

The Truck Driver is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of heavy rigid trucks to transport goods, agricultural supplies and equipment in support of NVD Fresh Produce's farming operations. The role ensures the timely collection, delivery and movement of goods while maintaining vehicle safety, operational efficiency and compliance with workplace health and safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Transport Operations
•	Operate heavy rigid trucks safely to transport goods, agricultural supplies and equipment. 
•	Load, secure and unload goods, materials and equipment in accordance with workplace procedures.
•	Ensure deliveries and collections are completed safely, efficiently and on schedule. 
Vehicle Maintenance and Compliance
•	Conduct routine pre-start and post-trip vehicle inspections. 
•	Report mechanical faults, maintenance requirements and safety issues promptly. 
•	Maintain vehicle cleanliness and ensure compliance with road transport and workplace safety requirements. 
•	Complete transport documentation and delivery records accurately. 
Farm Operations Support
•	Assist with loading and unloading activities as required. 
•	Support general farm logistics and transportation requirements during harvesting and production periods. 
•	Work collaboratively with farm managers and other employees to ensure efficient daily operations. 
Workplace Safety
•	Follow workplace health and safety procedures at all times. 
•	Ensure the safe handling and transportation of produce, equipment and materials. 
•	Maintain a professional and safety-focused approach while operating heavy vehicles. 

Qualifications and Skills

Applicants should possess one of the following:
•	A relevant AQF Certificate II qualification (or equivalent) together with at least 1 year's relevant post-qualification employment experience (20+ hours per week); or 
•	At least 2 years' relevant employment experience (10+ hours per week) in lieu of a formal qualification, together with an additional 2 years' relevant full-time employment experience.

In addition, applicants should demonstrate:
•	Experience operating heavy rigid trucks in an agricultural, farming, transport or logistics environment. 
•	A current Heavy Rigid (HR) Driver Licence is required. 
•	A Heavy Combination (HC) Driver Licence will be highly regarded.
•	Ability to perform routine vehicle safety inspections and report mechanical faults. 
•	Ability to transport goods safely and efficiently in accordance with workplace procedures.
•	Ability to maintain accurate transport and delivery records. 
•	Ability to follow work instructions and communicate effectively with supervisors and team members. 
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team. 
•	Commitment to workplace health and safety. 

How to apply:

Applications open on 10 July 2026 and close on 9 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.
